Critical UEFI Firmware Flaw Threatens Global Server Infrastructure

28 Oct 2026, 08:21 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Science Desk · Source: arstechnica.com

1 min read

Key takeaways

Image: arstechnica.com · Photo source · Cropped to 16:9; original source image

In this article
  1. Understanding the Vulnerability
  2. Impact and Mitigation

Understanding the Vulnerability

A high-severity vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-97631, has been identified in the TianoCore EDK II firmware codebase. With a severity rating of 9.5, the flaw resides in the PXE-Base Code driver, which handles network-based booting. An attacker with local network access can trigger a buffer overflow by sending oversized ICMP error messages, potentially executing malicious code at the CPU's most privileged level (Ring 0) during the boot process.

Impact and Mitigation

This flaw primarily affects enterprise servers and data centers utilizing network booting. Unlike consumer hardware booting from local disks, these systems are uniquely exposed. While no evidence suggests it serves as an initial entry point for network infiltration, it could facilitate privilege escalation. Administrators should contact hardware vendors for firmware updates and consider disabling network boot configurations as a temporary precaution. Details can be found at https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/10/code-execution-flaw-in-uefi-firmware-threatens-most-servers-on-planet-earth/
